In [[mathematics]], the '''Goncharov conjecture''' is a conjecture introduced by [[Alexander Goncharov|Goncharov]]{{sfnp|Goncharov|1995}} suggesting that the [[cohomology]] of certain [[Motivic cohomology|motivic complex]]es coincides with pieces of [[Algebraic K-theory|K-groups]]. It extends a conjecture due to [[Don Zagier|Zagier]].{{sfnp|Zagier|1991}}

==Statement==

Let <math>F</math> be a field. Goncharov defined the following complex called <math>\Gamma(F,n)</math> placed in degrees <math>[1,n]</math>:
:<math>\Gamma_F(n): \mathcal B_n(F)\to \mathcal B_{n-1}(F)\otimes F^\times_\mathbb Q\to\dots\to \Lambda^n F^\times_\mathbb Q. </math>

He conjectured that <math>i</math>-th cohomology of this complex is isomorphic to the motivic cohomology group <math>H^i_{mot}(F,\mathbb Q(n))</math>.
